title: Indexed transduction of a complete block
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $V,C$ be types, let $\mathit{visit}_i:V\times C\to V\times C$ be a local rule for each $i\in\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, let $\mathit{cell}$ assign an element of $C$ to each such index, and let $s$ be a table with values in $V$. Sweeping through the pairs $(i,\mathit{cell}(i))$ in increasing index order yields the table whose value at each $i$ is the first component of $\mathit{visit}_i(s(i),\mathit{cell}(i))$, together with the same ordered block in which each cell is replaced by the second component of that local-rule value.
hypotheses_covered: Family of local rules indexed by $\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$
Function assigning a cell in $C$ to each index
replaced:
Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mathit{visit}_i \colon V \times C \to V \times
C$ be a family of local rules indexed by $i \in \{0, \dots, k-1\}$, let
$\mathit{cell}$ assign a cell to each index, and let $s$ be an initial table.
Transducing, with the table-valued indexed transducer started at $s$, the
block listing every index $i$ exactly once in increasing order tagged with
$\mathit{cell}(i)$, yields the table $i \mapsto$ (new value of
$\mathit{visit}_i$ on $s(i)$ and $\mathit{cell}(i)$) together with the block
of rewritten tagged cells in the same order.
